first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6%, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) corroborate that simplifying onboarding/signup durably improves completion and activation without noted downside — this directly targets the observed regressions and supports sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is superficially attractive given competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but memory_73 explicitly warns it boosts acquisition while materially harming 30-day retention, conflicting with the long-term qualified revenue objective; I verify memory_73 to confirm this risk is genuine before ruling it out, and verify memory_86 since it's the strongest and most recent support for the chosen action given the current metric decline it's meant to address. I'm running this as a standard (not broad) experiment since it's a single week's slot and I want to confirm real-world effect size before wider rollout, and flagging the downstream value risk of the tempting-but-rejected pricing lever so it isn't quietly reconsidered later without re-examining retention tradeoffs.
